papers.title: Dynamical entropy and thermodynamics of causal diamonds
papers.abstract: arXiv:2610.22398v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the dynamical entropy of causal diamonds using Wald-Zoupas charges and fluxes on their null boundaries. For a chosen boundary symplectic potential, the boost charge defines an entropy made of an area term plus an expansion correction, which reduces to one quarter of the area at the edge on the diamond. In Einstein gravity, we find an exact balance law relating the entropy on any two cuts of the null boundary to a signed flux, so the entropy decreases only when this flux is non-negative. We obtain a linearised physical process first law without assuming a background Killing symmetry, both in the presence and absence of external matter; and extend it for semiclassical gravity based on the improved quantum null energy condition. We also examine causal diamonds in maximally symmetric spacetimes and in Einstein-scalar gravity.
papers.authors: Avik Chakraborty, Pratik K. Das, Manavendra Mahato

papers.title: Geodesics in Black-Hole Spacetimes: A Qualitative Classification Using Vieta's Formulae
papers.abstract: arXiv:2610.22399v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This monograph classifies the geodesics of the Schwarzschild, Kerr and Schwarzschild-de Sitter black holes without solving for their turning points. In all three spacetimes, the radial and polar motions are governed by polynomials whose coefficients depend only on the constants of motion, and the qualitative behavior of a geodesic is fixed by the pattern of their roots. We read this pattern directly off the coefficients, using Vieta's formulae together with the discriminant, Descartes' rule of signs, and the values of the polynomials at the horizons and at infinity. In Schwarzschild spacetime, the reciprocals of the radial roots of every non-radial geodesic add up to $1/(2M)$, which gives the third root of a bound orbit in closed form and the separatrix $p=6+2e$. In Kerr spacetime, the signs of the coefficients show that no radially bound orbit has $\varepsilon^2\geq1$ and that vortical geodesics, timelike or null, have no radial turning point; a positive discriminant is necessary but not sufficient for bound motion, and Descartes' rule applied at the event horizon gives the exact criterion. Spherical orbits and their stability, the equatorial ISCO and light rings, and the photon shell follow from the same relations. In Schwarzschild-de Sitter spacetime, the timelike radial polynomial is a quintic with exactly one negative root, a bound branch requires $\varepsilon^2+\Lambda L^2/3<1$, and both marginally stable circular orbits lie beyond $6M$. Most of these results are known; the aim is to show that a single, elementary algebraic route leads to all of them. The text is meant for graduate students who have taken a first course in general relativity, and each chapter ends with worked examples.
papers.authors: Oliver F. Piattella

papers.title: Dilaton-Axion Wormhole Partition Function Away from the BPS Endpoint
papers.abstract: arXiv:2610.22429v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: I determine the leading finite-radius correction to the two-boundary response of a charged axion wormhole near its BPS endpoint. With $\delta=a_*^2$, exact radial matching in a product axion--dilaton/saxion system gives a boundary eigenvalue that vanishes as $O(\delta)$ and an off-diagonal Hessian entry of order $O(\delta^2)$. Their combination produces a cross-boundary covariance linear in $\delta$, with a negative first sub-leading correction on the branch studied here. I determine the semiclassical range in which the quadratic approximation remains controlled and identify the first finite-radius angular resonance, $\delta^2\log(\delta/\delta_0)$. Under a uniform rescaling of all active charges, the coefficient of the linear cross-boundary response scales as the inverse square of the charge scale. I then average the inverse response over the chiral Gaussian ensemble describing the BPS endpoint. Boundary reduction preserves the hard-edge index. Multiplication by the matched BPS sector weight converts the normalized response into the leading finite-radius two-source coefficient.
papers.authors: Soo-Jong Rey

papers.title: Angular Momenta in $4+1$ Vacuum Critical Collapse
papers.abstract: arXiv:2610.22475v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate the critical collapse of gravitational waves that carry angular momenta. Working in five-dimensional vacuum Einstein gravity under an SU$(2)\times\mathbb Z_4$ symmetry ansatz, we numerically evolve several families of initial data near the threshold of black-hole formation. Near-critical data approaches the discretely self-similar Bizo\'n-Chmaj-Schmidt solution, which is irrotational. We find that the near-threshold mass scaling has a universal critical exponent, but the angular-momentum scaling has one of two critical exponents, depending on the family of initial data. The angular-momentum critical exponents are therefore not universal under this symmetry ansatz. Our results agree with predictions from perturbation theory about the critical solution.
papers.authors: Oscar J. C. Dias, Carsten Gundlach, Jorge E. Santos, Benson Way

papers.title: A non-prompt null ray cures its own singularity
papers.abstract: arXiv:2610.22478v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In AdS/CFT correlators, bulk cone singularities arise when two points that are timelike separated on the AdS boundary may be connected by a null geodesic through the bulk. We consider corrections to these correlators away from the $G_N\to 0$ limit arising from the backreaction of this null geodesic. A peculiar property of this geodesic is that it is not prompt, meaning that there exist points on it that are timelike separated. This implies that it may gravitationally affect itself. We show that this leads to an energy-dependent delay in the time elapsed along this geodesic. This coupled with possible inelastic effects due to gravitational radiation are the leading mechanisms that resolve the singularity. The resolved singularity is accompanied by oscillations and hence zeroes in the real and imaginary parts of the correlator. We comment on the role that additional inelastic effects play in damping these oscillations. Finally, we provide a concrete example in $2+1$D where we can compute the energy-dependent time delay effect explicitly by studying the boundary graviton mode.
papers.authors: Gauri Batra

papers.title: Modeling extreme mass-ratio inspirals in astrophysical and dark-matter environments
papers.abstract: arXiv:2610.22480v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Extreme mass-ratio inspirals offer a powerful probe of massive black holes and their environments, but interpreting their signals requires accurate models of orbital dynamics and radiation. Here we bring together advances in black-hole perturbation theory to establish a unified relativistic framework for adiabatic inspirals in perturbative astrophysical environments. Built on the modified Teukolsky formalism, the framework requires neither post-Newtonian nor slow-rotation approximations. As a first application, we calculate the leading cloud-induced corrections to gravitational-wave fluxes and conservative orbital dynamics for circular, equatorial inspirals around a rotating black hole surrounded by a synchronized ultralight scalar cloud, combining these corrections with the previously calculated scalar response. In our fiducial system, a cloud containing $10^{-4}$ of the black-hole mass produces about $-57.3$ radians of orbital dephasing over two years. The phase contributions from gravitational-wave flux corrections and background-induced orbital shifts each exceed the scalar contribution in magnitude and partially cancel, highlighting the need for coupled matter-gravity modeling. Extensible to other environments and modified gravity theories, our framework provides the relativistic inputs needed to assess detection losses and parameter biases, and to probe the nature of black-hole environments with future space-based gravitational-wave observations.
papers.authors: Dongjun Li, Hao-Jui Kuan, Colin Weller, Chaoyi Yang, Kelvin Ka-Ho Lam, Patrick Bourg, Adrian Ka-Wai Chung, Yanbei Chen, Nicol\'as Yunes, Huan Yang

papers.title: Topological Aspects of the $c=2$ Model in the Continuum and on the Lattice
papers.abstract: arXiv:2610.22485v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We discuss the continuum two-dimensional conformal field theory, whose target space is a two-torus. In addition to its standard zero-form internal symmetries, the model also has a $-1$-form symmetry associated with its $\theta$-parameter, which is also known as a background $B$-field. These symmetries combine into a higher group with anomalies. A spatially winding $B$-field generically breaks the spatial translation symmetry completely, and reduces the continuous target-space (internal) momentum symmetry to a (projectively realized) discrete subgroup. When $B$ varies linearly, a discrete translation subgroup survives, and it combines with the internal symmetry into a non-Abelian group, while the other translations survive as non-invertible symmetries. Even though the model lacks the standard spatial translation symmetry, the non-invertible translation symmetry explains why it is solvable via a Fourier decomposition. We then consider a lattice version of this system, using its modified Villain formulation. Surprisingly, all these subtleties in the symmetries of the continuum model exist on a finite lattice. Finally, we discuss various generalizations of this model, demonstrating that the phenomena we uncovered are more broadly valid.
papers.authors: Yichul Choi, Nathan Seiberg, Sahand Seifnashri, Wucheng Zhang

papers.title: Superstring theory in $AdS_5\times S^5$ background: half-BPS vertex operators
papers.abstract: arXiv:2610.22502v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we construct all vertex operators associated with the gravity supermultiplet in the $AdS_5 \times S^5$ background, relevant for worldsheet scattering amplitude computations, via global $PSU(2,2|4)$ transformations. Although one such operator was previously constructed in the pure spinor formalism using a special superspace parametrization, implementing the full global symmetries proved challenging due to the mixing of bosonic and fermionic coordinates. We resolve this issue by introducing a judicious sequence of reparametrizations that disentangle these coordinates. We then advance the formulation of superstring theory in this background by constructing the corresponding integrated vertex operators in both the pure spinor and the B-RNS-GSS formalisms.
papers.authors: Thiago Fleury, Lucas N. S. Martins, Dennis Zavaleta

papers.title: No cosmic horizons from a strengthened higher-dimensional strong energy condition
papers.abstract: arXiv:2610.22506v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Time-dependent supergravity compactifications lie beyond the setting of the Gibbons/Maldacena-Nu\~nez no-de Sitter theorem and can even support eternal cosmic acceleration, raising the question of whether they can also produce future cosmic horizons. For general higher-dimensional matter, the strong energy condition alone does not exclude such horizons. Here, we demonstrate that a theory fulfilling a strengthened version of the strong energy condition cannot be compactified down to a lower-dimensional theory able to support a future cosmic horizon. For 10d and 11d supergravities reduced to at least four large spacetime dimensions, this energy condition is fulfilled by the sources that already fulfill the strong energy condition in the higher-dimensional theory. Our assumption on the dimensional reduction is that it is performed on a smooth compact and boundaryless space.
papers.authors: Flavio Tonioni

papers.title: Perturbative Defect CFT Data in Scalar Models and Consistency Conditions
papers.abstract: arXiv:2610.22591v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We compute defect CFT data through $O(\epsilon)$ for scalar line defects in the $O(N)$, hypercubic, hypertetrahedral, $O(m)\times O(n)$ biconical, and $MN$ models in $d=4-\epsilon$. The $O(N)$ theory provides a benchmark; the datasets for the other four models are new. For the branches considered, we determine spectra, operator mixing, two- and three-point coefficients in a specified perturbative basis, and four-point functions with identical or paired external operators of integer dimension $n\leq2$ at $\epsilon=0$. We propose a framework for verifying perturbative defect CFT data by combining crossing symmetry, OPE reconstruction, and the applicable broken-symmetry integral identities. We also identify a new universal defect-direction sector whose one-loop data follow from the defect fixed-point equation. All applicable conditions are satisfied at the perturbative orders considered. The model data are collected in the supplemental notebook, defect_cft_data.nb.
papers.authors: Ziwen Kong

papers.title: Maximizing the spectral gap for free bosonic CFTs
papers.abstract: arXiv:2610.22633v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the spectral gap $\Delta_1$ of Narain CFTs, the smallest scaling dimension of a nonvacuum $U(1)^c_L\times U(1)^c_R$ primary, as a function on the Narain moduli space. Using the exceptional isomorphisms for $SO^+(2,2)$ and $SO^+(3,3)$, we prove the sharp bounds $\Delta_1\le 2/3$ at $c=2$ and $\Delta_1\le 3/4$ at $c=3$, with equality exactly at the $SU(3)_1$ and $SU(4)_1$ WZW models up to $O(c)\times O(c)$, and we describe local maxima of $\Delta_1$. For $4\le c\le 12$, we compare the Narain moduli space with the densest known Euclidean lattices: an arithmetic obstruction excludes five candidates, a computer-assisted classification shows that $E_8$, $K_{12}$, and $BW_{16}$ each admit a unique Narain structure up to lattice automorphisms, and a conceptual argument excludes the Leech lattice.
papers.authors: Hyeongjoe Chu, Yuchan Jung

papers.title: Primordial Power Spectrum from the Lensed CMB Temperature Spectrum using Iterative Delensing and Fourier Denoising
papers.abstract: arXiv:2610.22648v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The CMB power spectra are a strong probe of the primordial power spectrum (PPS) of the initial inflationary scalar perturbations. There are many proposed models, from the simpler power law form to various well motivated physical models that predict features in the PPS beyond the power law. Given the large parameter space of possible models, it is necessary to have model independent searches for such features. Weak gravitational lensing alters the CMB temperature power spectrum and can bias free form reconstructions of the primordial power spectrum (PPS) if not accounted for precisely, such as when using estimators like the Richardson-Lucy (RL) deconvolution algorithm. We build on our design of the Non linear Iterative Richardson Lucy (NIRL) estimator that updates the lensing contribution using the freeform PPS recovered at the previous iteration, making it truly model independent in the PPS domain while accounting for lensing. Inspired by signal processing and Fourier filtering techniques from radio interferometry, we also design a Fourier space iterative low pass filter (FLIP) to suppress noise overfitting in NIRL reconstructions. We demonstrate the performance of NIRL-FLIP on a range of simulated PPS models with bootstrap estimates of reconstruction uncertainty obtained from simulated realizations, and show that both our estimator and regularization are robust, accurate and precise, and are able to both reduce lensing induced reconstruction bias and suppress noise overfitting by a significant factor in Fourier space. We provide a detailed description of these results and recommend its utility for future model independent searches for hints of novel physics in the form of deviations from a power law PPS. This can further assist in precise and accurate testing of inflation models, in conjunction with joint cosmological parameter estimation.
papers.authors: Rajorshi Sushovan Chandra, Debarshi Mukherjee, Tarun Souradeep

papers.title: Functional Analysis of Widefield Radio Interferometry
papers.abstract: arXiv:2610.22752v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Radio interferometry relies on reconstruction techniques to form images from discrete visibility measurements. As instruments encompass wider fields of view, the nuance of that reconstruction can lead to geometrical errors in the image. As a result, the estimation of the flux density of sources can change. We derive the full functional analysis of widefield radio interferometry to provide a foundation for investigating geometry-based errors. We use this framework to investigate three examples: 1) deconvolution errors resulting from a minor iteration, 2) gridding errors resulting from excluding primary beam sidelobes, and 3) w-term errors resulting from omitting the non-coplanar dimension on a 2 min near-zenith transit. We use their adjoint operator descriptions to simulate each of the three cases for two fields using the Murchison Widefield Array. While the estimated errors on the flux density of reconstructed sources are small, overall errors depend on the field observed. For our two fields, we find fractional flux density errors up to 5% due to deconvolution, 0.1% due to gridding, and 10% due to non-coplanarity. Our operator formalism can be used to investigate many other forms of image reconstruction errors.
papers.authors: Nichole Barry, Jaiden Cook, Cathryn Trott, Tiasha Biswas,  Nazeef

papers.title: Hidden Supersymmetry in AdS/QCD models for Fermions
papers.abstract: arXiv:2610.22806v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We show that the chiral modes splitted from the Dirac equation satisfying Schrodinger-like equations in the context of deformed AdS/QCD model are isospectral, since the chiral effective potentials are SUSY partners. In particular, we show how to perform truncations of these potentials that preserve isospectrality of the chiral modes. Following this prescription, we compare a quadratic approximation of the deformed AdS model with the dressed soft wall model for fermions and show how the spectra of both models can coincide.
papers.authors: Rafael A. Costa-Silva, Henrique Boschi-Filho

papers.title: Geometric Capture and Optical Critical Curves of Purely Electric, Magnetic and Dyonic Black Holes in Einstein-Euler-Heisenberg Theory
papers.abstract: arXiv:2610.22814v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We examine background null capture in the electric, magnetic, and dyonic solutions of Einstein gravity coupled to a quartic Euler-Heisenberg-type electromagnetic Lagrangian. The calculation uses the exact hypergeometric electric solution, the closed-form magnetic solution, and a numerical dyonic solution. Relative to the Reissner-Nordstr\"om value at fixed total charge, the EEH correction increases the geometric critical impact parameter in the parameter ranges considered. For the purely magnetic case, the disappearance of the two outer horizons can expose an additional capture barrier and thus forms an unstable circular orbit with a very small radius. In the dyonic case, for a fixed magnetic-to-electric charge ratio, the behavior is consistent with that of the pure electric solution while preserving the phase transition between single- and multi-horizon black hole phases. Moreover, when the coupling parameter is fixed, the effect of the magnetic-to-electric charge ratio depends on the electric charge. The present findings establish that the multi-horizon phase can impart pronounced signatures to geometric photon observables, whereas, in the off-transition regime, the purely electric, purely magnetic, and dyonic solutions remain characterized by clearly distinguishable trends.
papers.authors: Yong-Zhuang Li, An-Hao Xu, Haoyuan Luo, Xiao Yan Chew

papers.title: Analytic and numerical study of dark matter halos in the Horndeski theory
papers.abstract: arXiv:2610.22819v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The models of modified gravity that can explain the late-time accelerated expansion of the Universe must pass the local tests of gravity, introducing a screening mechanism so that any additional fifth force in gravity is suppressed at stellar scales. Dark matter halos, in contrast, by their extendedness in scale, may exhibit a transition of screening to small scales, providing a probe of modified gravity and the origin of the late-time acceleration. We perform comprehensive studies of dark matter halos with Vainshtein screening in the Horndeski theory. Given that dark matter is cold and a dark matter halo is spherically symmetric, we analytically clarify the conditions for the halo profile under which the Vainshtein screening works effectively. We find that the Vainshtein screening is less effective even within the Vainshtein radius as the profile approaches a core-like structure around the center of a halo, which motivates us to postulate that some features owing to the fifth force can survive during the dynamical evolution of a halo. We numerically examine our postulate by a $N$-body simulation for an isolated halo with the assumption of Newtonian two-body interactions with the spherical external fifth force. We make use of three proxies of the mass through hydrostatic dynamics, the Jeans equation, and gravitational lensing, all of which must be identical in the case of Newtonian gravity as a weak-field approximation to General Relativity. We find that these proxies can be biased relative to each other at a (quasi) equilibrium, quantitatively indicating that the fiducial model of gravity is not Newtonian. Our result affirmatively suggests that multiple mass proxies from observations are capable of testing gravity on halo scales.
papers.authors: Kohei Onoda, Shun Arai, Daisuke Yamauchi, Shuichiro Yokoyama, Shogo Masaki, Kenji Hasegawa

papers.title: Asymmetric multiscalar fixed points from equiangular tight frames
papers.abstract: arXiv:2610.22923v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In their work on multiscalar RG flows, Rychkov and Stergiou posed the question of whether there exist real fixed points of the one-loop renormalization group for scalar field theories in $d=4-\epsilon$ which respect no extra symmetry beyond the universal $\mathbb{Z}_2$ field inversion. In this note, we report on a construction of a large number of such fixed points in the theory of $22001$ scalar fields, thus resolving the question. The construction uses the geometry of an equiangular tight frame in order to reduce the (up to two-loop) fixed point equation to a two-dimensional space of couplings without assuming any extra symmetry. The main technical hurdle is then to establish the existence of such a frame whose corresponding lines preserve no symmetry. This can be achieved using the Steiner frame construction of Fickus, Mixon, and Tremain.
papers.authors: Christopher Beem

papers.title: An Exact No-Rotation Criterion in Circular Stationary Spacetimes
papers.abstract: arXiv:2610.23088v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We derive an exact no-rotation criterion for circular, stationary, axisymmetric spacetimes from Einstein's field equations. Its integrated form excludes frame dragging when the weighted matter contribution is nonpositive, the boundary flux vanishes, and the bulk integrals converge. For opposing momentum sources, a finite-region argument excludes frame dragging in a regular region when its boundary values tend uniformly to zero. Time-independent minimally coupled canonical real scalars illustrate the opposing sign, whereas harmonic complex fields can supply angular momentum. In the Barriola--Vilenkin scalar model, the application covers global helical fields with general meridional amplitudes, including possible higher-winding monopole configurations. A persistent vacuum field at an asymptotically conical end locks the phase pattern to the asymptotic frame, excluding horizonless rotation. A nonzero transverse horizon amplitude also synchronizes the horizon with that frame and makes the exterior nonrotating.
papers.authors: Xiao-Yin Pan, Qing-hai Wang

papers.title: Environment-induced topological reconstruction of black-hole thermodynamics
papers.abstract: arXiv:2610.23101v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Thermodynamic topology describes black-hole (BH) equilibria as zeros, or defects, of a vector field built from the off-shell free energy. Studies with surrounding matter find that the topological class is unchanged, but not how the matter's spatial distribution affects individual equilibria. We ask whether the position of a localized environment can reorganize these equilibria at fixed total topological number. We model the environment as a radially localized energy bump peaked at $a_m$ and add its exterior energy to the generalized off-shell free energy. As $a_m$ varies, defects migrate and are created or annihilated in opposite-charge pairs, a process we call topological reconstruction. It changes the number and stability of equilibrium branches but preserves the total topological number, provided no zero crosses the boundary of the physical domain. We find this in Schwarzschild, Schwarzschild-AdS, Reissner-Nordstr\"om, and Reissner-Nordstr\"om-AdS BHs, with critical positions and required strength that depend on the background. In our examples, the required environmental energy ranges from below $1\%$ of the BH mass to a value comparable to it. The model is an effective fixed-background description without backreaction. Within it, the total topological number cannot capture the environmental response; local defects must be tracked.
papers.authors: Xinyu Zhou, Chen Lan, Zhen-Ming Xu

papers.title: Uniqueness of Static Black Holes in Lovelock Gravity
papers.abstract: arXiv:2610.23133v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Black hole uniqueness is one of the fundamental predictions of general relativity: the spherically symmetric Schwarzschild--Tangherlini spacetime is the unique regular, asymptotically flat, static vacuum black hole solution of Einstein's equations. We show that an analogous result holds perturbatively in Lovelock gravity. Assuming the appropriate positive-mass rigidity statement, any regular, asymptotically flat, static vacuum black hole solution of Lovelock gravity on a generic branch admitting a regular Taylor expansion about general relativity is uniquely determined, at fixed ADM mass, by the corresponding spherically symmetric Lovelock black hole solution. In particular, Einstein--Gauss--Bonnet gravity admits no distinct nonspherical static branch perturbatively connected to Schwarzschild--Tangherlini, and the unique solution is Boulware--Deser. The same recursive mechanism extends to the full Lovelock class. Our result shows that static black hole uniqueness can extend beyond general relativity and is not a property peculiar to the Einstein equations.
papers.authors: Chanchal Sharma, Sudipta Sarkar

papers.title: Consistency Checks for {\Lambda} positive Quantum Cosmology
papers.abstract: arXiv:2610.23168v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper we improve and further analyze the recently derived quantum gravity equations which apply in accelerating cosmological spacetimes and whose solutions re-sum leading logarithms from all orders of perturbation theory. We show the consistency of these upgraded equations against 1-loop non-trivial exact perturbative computations. The upgraded equations retain their remarkably simple form.
papers.authors: S. P. Miao, N. C. Tsamis, R. P. Woodard

papers.title: Conservative Orbital Resonance Networks as Local Environmental Diagnostics for Extreme Mass Ratio Inspirals
papers.abstract: arXiv:2610.23174v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: LLow order orbital resonances provide localized probes of the conservative geometry sampled by extreme mass ratio inspirals. We study fixed eccentricity and inclination slices of the ordered $3{:}2$, $5{:}3$, and $2{:}1$ polar to radial resonance surfaces in source consistent anisotropic black hole environments, treating rotation strictly to first order. A horizon regularized Dehnen sequence produces unequal resonance displacements, reaching $-7.17\%$, $-5.45\%$, and $-3.94\%$ in a fixed global benchmark. After matching both the total environmental mass and the enclosed mass at $10M_\bullet$, we compare Dehnen and Einasto inspired families. Two dimensionless network spacing ratios are organized primarily by the local logarithmic enclosed mass slope: for the common $\beta=2$ regularization their maximum cross family departure from a shared linear relation is $4.1\times10^{-4}$, while varying the horizon taper through $\beta=2$--$4$ increases the departure to at most $2.1\times10^{-3}$. The unequal ordering of the three resonance displacements holds at every point of a directly evaluated finite eccentricity and inclination grid. A six observable conservative response analysis is numerically full rank but strongly ill conditioned and nearly aligned with orbital nuisance directions. The result therefore establishes local conservative profile sensitivity, not unique tomography or a detector level parameter recovery forecast.
papers.authors: Mona Kumari, Anirudh Pradhan, K. Ghaderi, Javlon Rayimbaev

papers.title: Optical conductivity of holographic striped superconductors
papers.abstract: arXiv:2610.23184v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Based on a holographic model exhibiting Mott-like insulating behavior on an ionic lattice, we construct a holographic striped superconductor (SSC), which is characterized by the interplay between the charge density wave (CDW) and superconductivity (SC). We present the phase diagram on the $e$-$T$ plane, where the SSC phase emerges within an intermediate window of $e$, revealing both cooperative and competitive relations between the CDW order and SC order. For small charge $e$, the system undergoes the phase transition from metallic phase to CDW phase, and then to SSC phase upon cooling; while for large $e$, it transitions from metallic phase to SC phase directly, and then to SSC phase. We compute the optical conductivity of the system for these two cases and demonstrate its distinct behavior. It turns out that the imaginary part of the conductivity exhibits a divergent behavior below the critical temperature $T_{\mathrm{SSC}}$ along both pathways, so that the superconductivity of SSC phase is justified for the first time in the holographic framework. Along the CDW-to-SSC pathway the pseudogap and the pinning effect are inherited from the CDW phase, whereas along the SC-to-SSC pathway the spontaneous stripe strongly suppresses the coherent normal-fluid channel while the superfluid pole is enhanced. In addition, we demonstrate the commensurate lock-in behavior of the striped superconductor in the $p$-$T$ diagram.
papers.authors: Fang-jing Cheng, Kai Li, Yi Ling, Meng-He Wu

papers.title: Simulating dust collapse: the impact of gauge choices on primordial black hole formation
papers.abstract: arXiv:2610.23218v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate why numerical relativity simulations of dust collapse in a matter-dominated era frequently fail before primordial black hole formation due to numerical limitations and inappropriate gauge choices. Using 3-dimensional fully non-linear simulations of a dust fluid, we detail the advantages of advanced numerical methods and the impact of the lapse and shift evolution equations. The challenge is twofold: 1) conventional lapse slicing evolution equations, highly effective in typical black hole simulations, must be adapted in a cosmological context. We demonstrate how different proposed lapse evolution equations perform, enabling fair comparison, and propose our own. 2) The shift evolution equation's role is to spread out the numerical grid observers for a stable simulation. However, the Gamma-driver evolution fails when confronted with shell-focussing of the dust fluid. We show how the shift damping choice depends on the resolution of the shell-focusing region, suggesting that future work should have spatially varying damping. Our improved gauge choices allow simulations to evolve significantly further and potentially reach black hole formation. The best-performing simulations reach close proximity to a black hole; however, further work on the gauge choice is required for this to be stable.
papers.authors: Robyn L. Munoz, Christian T. Byrnes, Marco Bruni, Ian Hawke

papers.title: Exact $T\bar{T}$-Like Flows in Nonlinear Electrodynamics
papers.abstract: arXiv:2610.23281v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We derive an exact nonperturbative $T\bar T$-like flow for the class of one-scale, self-dual nonlinear electrodynamics theories admitting a Courant--Hilbert representation. The flow has a universal parametric form in terms of the defining Courant--Hilbert function and, on any physical branch where the relevant invariant map is invertible, becomes an autonomous function of the two quadratic stress-tensor invariants, $\partial_\lambda\mathcal L=X\,\mathcal F(Y/X)$. The function $\mathcal F$ is model dependent, and global autonomy is assumed when the invariant map is one-to-one. Born--Infeld theory yields a quadratic stress-tensor flow, whereas the causal Russo--Townsend logarithmic model gives an exact nonlinear expression involving the Lambert $W$ function whose weak-field expansion reproduces the known perturbative result. We also establish the equivalence with the Russo--Townsend auxiliary-field formulation. These results provide an exact construction of autonomous irrelevant flows for a broad, explicitly specified class of self-dual nonlinear electrodynamics theories.
papers.authors: Zahra Pezhman, H. Babaei-Aghbolagh, Komeil Babaei Velni

papers.title: Foreground Groups and Host-Galaxy Geometry in the Dispersion-Measure Scatter of Fast Radio Bursts
papers.abstract: arXiv:2610.23333v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Localized fast radio bursts (FRBs) show substantial scatter in dispersion measure (DM) about the mean cosmic DM--redshift relation, also known as the Macquart relation. Both foreground structure and host galaxies contribute to this scatter. In this work, we examine foreground tracers and host galaxy properties using a parent catalog of 136 localized FRBs with measured DMs and spectroscopic host redshifts. Among 77 FRBs within the Gfinder footprint, DM excess relative to a fixed Macquart mean increases with foreground group count excess, with a Spearman coefficient of 0.459. Adding the foreground term to a mean host baseline reduces the leave-one-out root mean square error (RMSE) and mean absolute error (MAE) in extragalactic DM by \(13.0\%\) and \(7.5\%\), respectively. For 20 of these FRBs with optical host axis ratio measurements, adding a foreground term calibrated on the other 57 FRBs to the host shape model reduces the observer-frame leave-one-out RMSE from \(76.3\) to \(64.0~\mathrm{pc\,cm^{-3}}\) and MAE from \(54.2\) to \(50.2~\mathrm{pc\,cm^{-3}}\). And the in-sample residual standard deviation in the host rest frame decreases by \(20.2\%\). Idealized galaxy models based on the Milky Way electron density distribution produce DM changes with inclination comparable to the fitted amplitude under the adopted assumptions.
papers.authors: Jiale Wang, Taotao Fang

papers.title: Scalar Casimir Effect from Bilocal Correlations in a Wormhole Foam
papers.abstract: arXiv:2610.23369v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We determine how spatially bilocal correlations induced by a dilute ensemble of virtual Euclidean wormholes modify the scalar Casimir interaction between parallel Dirichlet plates. From the leading monopole action, we isolate an equal-Euclidean-time sector and construct a point-throat, first-order matched spectator model with fixed foam statistics. Global two-plate inclusion-exclusion over all mouth-pair center positions yields a continuous fixed-separation kernel free of the logarithmic image structures produced by a restricted translation sector. The kernel is quadratically suppressed at coincidence, changes sign near 0.695 plate spacings, and tends to a positive large-separation plateau. Averaging over truncated-Gaussian, log-normal, and Gamma distributions with a common relative width yields closely spaced energy curves but a finite shape dependence. Differentiating the dimensional energy at fixed ensemble parameters gives a leading-order pressure threshold of 0.05 in the large-separation limit. In the truncated-Gaussian scan extending to twelve plate spacings, an amplitude of 0.06 yields a crossover near a separation ratio of 3.17, whereas amplitudes of 0.02 and 0.04 remain attractive and 0.05 is critical. The scalar cavity therefore provides a scale-selective probe of spatial bilocality whose leading boundary response can change sign within the declared model.
papers.authors: Celio R. Muniz, M. C. Ara\'{u}jo, Edson Otoniel, Jonathan A. Rebou\c{c}as

papers.title: Spinors, Doppelg\"angers and the Non-Perturbative Classical Double Copy
papers.abstract: arXiv:2610.23384v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop a geometric and spinorial formulation of the non-perturbative classical double copy between the Corrigan--Fairlie--'t Hooft--Wilczek sector of complexified SU(2) Yang--Mills theory and four-dimensional conformally flat gravity. We identify the gauge potential with the positive-chiral spin connection of the conformally flat metric, establishing an exact relation between the Yang--Mills field strength and the chiral projection of the Riemann tensor. This provides a four-dimensional realisation of the doppelg\"anger viewpoint, in which gauge and gravitational fields arise from different interpretations of common connection data. Within this sector, the sourceless Yang--Mills equations require constant scalar curvature, explaining the shared nonlinear scalar equation and extending the gravitational correspondence from traceless matter to matter with constant energy--momentum trace. By representing adjoint colour indices as symmetric pairs of spinor indices, we derive exact relations mapping the gauge field-strength spinors to the scalar-curvature and trace-free Ricci components of the gravitational curvature. These relations retain nontrivial curvature information despite the vanishing Weyl tensor. We illustrate the construction using anti-de Sitter and de Sitter spacetimes, together with $\mathrm{AdS}_{3}\times\mathbb{R}$ supported by a scalar field, demonstrating the extension to matter with nonzero constant trace
papers.authors: Kymani Armstrong-Williams

papers.title: Topological Defects in Cosmic Shear
papers.abstract: arXiv:2610.23401v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this work, we present a novel approach for extracting cosmological information from cosmic shear maps based on topological defects in the shear orientation field. These defects are defined purely by the phase structure of the shear field and are therefore complementary to conventional weak lensing statistics that primarily probe amplitude information. We characterise their statistical properties, including number densities, spatial clustering, and the convergence distribution at defect locations, and demonstrate with Fisher analyses under idealised and realistic survey conditions that topological defect statistics provide a valuable and complementary source of cosmological information. With Euclid-like simulated data, the inclusion of defect statistics leads to constraints on $\Omega_{\rm m}$ and $\sigma_8$ that are up to 3.9 times tighter than those obtained from the convergence two-point correlation function alone.
papers.authors: Jiachen Bai, Benjamin Giblin, Andy Taylor

papers.title: Compensator-free $\mathcal N=2$ extension of ModMax and scalar propagation
papers.abstract: arXiv:2610.23447v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We construct a compensator-free $\mathcal N=2$ superconformal and electric--magnetic duality-invariant extension of ModMax electrodynamics in ordinary flat superspace. The action is built entirely from the Abelian vector multiplet, using a derivative composite of its field strength, and the self-duality equation is solved to all orders as a formal series in the coupling. Upon setting the additional $\mathcal N=1$ chiral multiplet to zero, the action is equivalent off shell to the $\mathcal N=1$ ModMax action of Bandos, Lechner, Sorokin and Townsend through a local vector-prepotential redefinition. Since the complex scalar of the $\mathcal N=2$ multiplet is set to zero in this reduction, we add one superconformal interaction that leaves the reduction unchanged and is chosen to ensure causal scalar propagation. On constant non-null electromagnetic backgrounds with vanishing scalar expectation value, the higher-order scalar coefficients are fixed by requiring the scalar quadratic action to satisfy the stress-tensor square-root flow, modulo equations of motion and a total derivative. We determine the quadratic action of the full multiplet on these backgrounds to all orders. Its analytic continuation to finite $\gamma\geq0$ gives causal scalar propagation, with transverse speed squared $e^{-\gamma}$ and unit longitudinal speed, the ModMax photon cones, luminal gauginos with positive kinetic coefficients, and auxiliary fields with algebraic equations of motion.
papers.authors: Ariunzul Davgadorj

papers.title: Near-Extremal Black-Hole Formation Observed from Null Infinity
papers.abstract: arXiv:2610.23486v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We identify near-extremal black-hole formation directly from observables at future null infinity. Fully nonlinear evolutions of the spherically symmetric Einstein--Maxwell--charged scalar system in 3+1 dimensions form black holes with charge-to-mass ratios up to 0.993 from regular, horizon-free, superextremal initial data. Quasinormal frequencies and redshift decay independently recover the near-extremal charge-to-mass ratio. Critical mass scaling is recovered at null infinity and charge scaling at the apparent horizon. The charged scalar Newman--Penrose quantity obeys an asymptotic balance law that replaces the conservation law of the neutral theory.
papers.authors: Thomas M\"adler, Radouane Gannouji, Steven L. Liebling, Emanuel Gallo

papers.title: Can coupled thawing quintessence reproduce DESI DR2? A test with two potentials
papers.abstract: arXiv:2610.23497v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: DESI DR2 favours dark energy whose equation of state evolves crossing $w=-1$ in the past. Coupled quintessence can produce such an apparent phantom crossing without a phantom field, since a coupled dark sector analysed under the assumption of separate conservation yields an effective equation of state below $-1$. We test whether this mechanism can reproduce the DESI result, using two thawing potentials, a cosine and a double-exponential hilltop, confronted with DESI DR2 BAO, Planck PR4 and three supernova compilations. Both models improve on $\Lambda$CDM by $\Delta\chi^2 = 5$--$15$, recovering $64$--$92\%$ of the improvement achieved by $w_0w_a$CDM. They track the $w_0w_a$CDM equation of state at $z\lesssim0.4$ but cross the phantom divide later, near $z\simeq1$ rather than $z\simeq0.4$--$0.5$. The coupling is bounded at $|\beta|<0.073$ ($95\%$), and the two potentials agree on it to within $0.15\sigma$. They differ instead in the equation of state they can reach: the cosine comes closer to the evolution preferred by DESI and is weakly preferred by the fit. The coupling posterior is bimodal, with modes at $\beta\simeq\pm0.05$; only the negative mode produces the crossing, and it is the higher of the two in every analysis. In conclusion, the data favour the coupled quintessence phantom crossing but do not yet require it.
papers.authors: Jhananii Yuvaraj Babu, Luca Amendola

papers.title: When Conformal Interfaces Become Logarithmic
papers.abstract: arXiv:2610.23509v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We construct conformal interfaces having defect conformal manifolds between two-dimensional rational CFTs, at least one of which is non-unitary. In a continuous family, interfaces with real and complex spectra can be marginally deformed to each other via their defect moduli parameters. An exceptional point then arises along the trajectory in the conformal manifold, where two interface operators with complex conjugate weights coalesce into a logarithmic pair. We reconstruct the entire trajectory of this novel spectral collision, independently, from self-annulus partition functions and bulk two point correlators in the presence of the interfaces.
papers.authors: Jin Chen

papers.title: Timelike entanglement entropy with gravitational anomaly from complexified geometry
papers.abstract: arXiv:2610.23514v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate the timelike entanglement entropy (TEE) in a two-dimensional conformal field theory with a gravitational anomaly, $c_L\neq c_R$, dual to topologically massive gravity in AdS$_3$. Holographically, the TEE is determined by the on-shell action of a massive spinning particle on a single complex geodesic anchored at the endpoints of the timelike interval. This action consists of the complex geodesic length and the twist of a parallel-transported normal frame. We carry out the computation in Poincar\'e AdS$_3$, non-extremal and extremal rotating BTZ backgrounds, and provide an equivalent Chern-Simons derivation in which the bulk connection stays real while only the saddle of the Wilson-line probe becomes complex. In each case, the holographic result matches the corresponding TEE in dual field theory. The real part of the TEE is fixed unambiguously whereas its imaginary part depends on the boundary $i\epsilon$ prescription and the orientation of the interval. In the bulk, the dependence on orientation reflects an ambiguity in the choice of framing. Along the complex geodesic, the residual frame group becomes $SO(2,\mathbb C)\simeq\mathbb C^*$, so the endpoint conditions determine the frame twist only up to integer multiples of $2\pi i$. The difference between the two orientations, $\frac{c_L-c_R}{6}\,i\pi$, is fixed entirely by the gravitational anomaly and persists for the R\'enyi pseudo-entropies.
papers.authors: Minwoo Lim, Himanshu Parihar, Junggi Yoon

papers.title: The metric-affine $\mathring{R}^2$ scalaron: parameter-free inflation
papers.abstract: arXiv:2610.23522v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present a model of slow-roll inflation in metric-affine gravity, where the connection is independent of the metric. We require that the Einstein-Hilbert term is the only operator that breaks three out of four shift-symmetries of the connection, and impose them on the metric-affine Starobinsky term $\alpha R(\Gamma)^2$. This replaces it by $\alpha\mathring{R}^2$, the square of the invariant part of the scalar curvature. The theory propagates only the graviton and one healthy scalar, the metric-affine $\mathring{R}^2$ scalaron. Its potential approaches a plateau polynomially, $U\simeq U_0(1-\mu^2/\chi^2)$, with $\mu=\sqrt{6}\,M_P$ fixed by the curvature of the connection. Once $\alpha\simeq2\times10^{8}$ is set by the scalar amplitude, the model has no free parameters. It predicts $n_s\simeq1-3/(2N_*)$ and $r\simeq2\sqrt3\,N_*^{-3/2}$ at leading order in $N_*$, and $n_s=0.968$--$0.974$ and $r=0.011$-$0.008$ with exact slow-roll for $N_*=50$-$60$ $e$-folds. These values agree with current data, and $r$ is within reach of the next generation of $B$-mode measurements.
papers.authors: Christian Dioguardi

papers.title: Renormalization Group Domain Walls from Phantom Symmetries
papers.abstract: arXiv:2610.23529v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop a systematic construction of renormalization group (RG) domain walls between two-dimensional rational conformal field theories. Using phantom currents, we consider an auxiliary chiral extension linked to the folded ultraviolet--infrared theory by a topological interface. The construction of RG walls then reduces to identifying suitable automorphism-twisted Cardy states in the auxiliary theory. We find two such types of automorphisms: outer automorphisms exchanging identical current algebra factors, as in Gaiotto's construction, and continuous inner automorphisms generated by the zero modes of spin-one phantom currents. In the latter case, the RG domain walls generically admit a continuous defect conformal manifold. We further show that, when an RG flow can be orbifolded to another one, the orbifold may lift defect conformal moduli of the RG brane constructed using inner automorphisms. The two types of RG branes can then be mapped to each other via a topological interface defined by the orbifold. We demonstrate the two types of RG brane construction via various examples of flows between non-unitary minimal models, from parafermions to minimal models, and between generalized parafermions. Many physical observables of the RG walls are computed non-perturbatively, including boundary entropies and spectra, and UV--IR operator mixings. We also find interesting nontrivial boundary monodromy: a closed cycle in the defect conformal moduli space can carry an RG domain wall into other distinct non-trivial conformal interfaces.
papers.authors: Jin Chen

papers.title: Possible detection of Baryon Acoustic Oscillations imprinted in the HI sources from the FASHI catalog
papers.abstract: arXiv:2610.23564v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Motivated by curiosity as to whether the observed Universe at low redshifts is well described by the concordance cosmological model, we investigate the large scale angular clustering of extragalactic neutral hydrogen HI sources in the local Universe. Using the second data release of the FAST All Sky HI Survey (FASHI), we analyze a sample of 142,204 HI sources up to $z<0.09$, with a median redshift of $\bar{z} = 0.034$, covering $\sim 40\%$ of the sky. We compute the 2-point angular correlation function, $w(\theta)$, and estimate its covariance using an analytical Gaussian model. We report the possible detection of a broad angular Baryon Acoustic Oscillation (BAO) signal, peaking near $50^\circ$. A comparison between a 5th-order polynomial fit and a quadratic baseline yields $\Delta \chi^2 = 9.06$ for $\Delta \mathrm{dof} = 3$ (difference of 3 degrees of freedom), corresponding to a nominal $1.9\,\sigma$ significance for a non-monotonic feature in $w(\theta)$ relative to the monotonic quadratic baseline, although this result alone does not establish a BAO detection. Our analyses show that, due to the projection effect, the expected transverse BAO scale shifts from $64^\circ$ in an infinitesimally thin redshift bin to $52^\circ$ in a bin of thickness $\Delta z = 0.09$, like the data we study, a value close to where our detection peaks, i.e., $\sim 50^\circ$. Furthermore, comparisons with an ensemble of lognormal mocks show that the observed broad bump is consistent with statistical fluctuations at the $1\sigma$ level, meaning that current uncertainties prevent us from unequivocally establishing it as a cosmological signal. Comprehensively, our study establishes a valuable observational baseline for wide-field HI surveys, showing the potential to trace primordial acoustic features even in the low redshift regime, where the transverse BAO signal is dominated by projection effects.
papers.authors: Felipe Avila, Camila Franco, Armando Bernui

papers.title: Galaxy bias of radio AGN and star-forming galaxies from MIGHTEE and CMB lensing
papers.abstract: arXiv:2610.23567v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Radio galaxies play a significant role in galaxy evolution through feedback mechanisms, making it important to characterize the environments in which they reside. We measure the cross-correlation between the positions of radio sources in the MIGHTEE survey and cosmic microwave background lensing measurements from the Atacama Cosmology Telescope over $20\ {\rm deg}^2$ to flux densities $S_{\rm 1.4\,GHz}>40\ {\rm \mu Jy}$, detecting the signal at $\sim4\sigma$ significance. By combining this with auto-correlation measurements of low- and high-redshift radio samples, we constrain the redshift evolution of the galaxy bias parameter, $b(z)$. Fitting different models for the redshift evolution of the bias, we find that both a model inversely proportional to the linear growth factor, $b(z) = (1.63^{+0.19}_{-0.22})/D(z)$, and a model where bias grows linearly with redshift, $b(z) = (0.49^{+0.44}_{-0.32}) + (1.62^{+0.37}_{-0.51})z$, provide comparably good fits to the data, with the current measurements unable to distinguish between them. Using a radio luminosity function, we estimate the fraction of sources that are active galactic nuclei (AGNs) or star-forming galaxies (SFGs) as a function of redshift, and model the individual contributions of AGNs and SFGs to the total bias. This approach allows us to measure the bias of AGNs and SFGs without individual source classifications. Though no single model is favoured significantly, the best-fitting model gives $b_{\rm AGN}(z) = (2.60^{+0.65}_{-0.91})/D(z)$ compared to $b_{\rm SFG}(z) = (0.52^{+0.47}_{-0.34})/D(z)$. Incorporating SFG bias measurements from previous work as a prior tightens these constraints to $b_{\rm AGN}(z) = (1.96^{+0.37}_{-0.40})/D(z)$ and $b_{\rm SFG}(z) = (0.90^{+0.06}_{-0.06})/D(z)$.
papers.authors: Joel Hamlett, Catherine L. Hale, Matt J. Jarvis, David Alonso, S. Lyla Jung, Natalia Stylianou, Rohan G. Varadaraj

papers.title: Holographic two-point functions across a PT symmetry-breaking transition
papers.abstract: arXiv:2610.23580v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In parity-time (PT)-symmetric non-Hermitian systems, an exceptional point, where eigenvalues and eigenvectors coalesce, typically separates a real spectrum from complex-conjugate eigenvalues. In logarithmic conformal field theories (LCFTs), such an exceptional point appears in the spectrum of scaling dimensions. Holographic models of LCFTs, such as the dipole model, are built exactly at this point. Here, we deform the holographic dipole model so that its two coalescing scaling dimensions split into either two real ones or a complex-conjugate pair. We obtain the renormalized two-point functions in closed form. They change continuously from a linear combination of two power laws, through the logarithmic form of the LCFT at the exceptional point, to log-periodic oscillations. For any pair of scalar primary operators with real mixing under dilatations, the conformal Ward identities fix this form up to two normalization constants, which the holographic dictionary determines. In PT-symmetric theories with such a dilatation operator, real and complex-conjugate scaling dimensions correspond to the PT-unbroken and PT-broken phases. In the BTZ black hole at finite temperature, the difference between the quasinormal frequencies associated with the two scaling dimensions changes from purely imaginary to purely real across the real-to-complex spectral transition. Correspondingly, the linear response changes from overdamped to underdamped, with critical damping at the exceptional point.
papers.authors: Zuo Wang, Liang He

papers.title: Alleviating cosmological strong coupling with torsion in regularized 4D Einstein-Gauss-Bonnet gravity
papers.abstract: arXiv:2610.23628v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The four-dimensional scalar-tensor theory obtained by conformally regularizing the Gauss-Bonnet term has a vanishing kinetic term for the scalar perturbation mode on its late-time de Sitter attractor, signaling strong coupling. We show that, when the regularization is carried out in Riemann-Cartan geometry, the resulting theory admits de Sitter attractors with trace torsion on which this kinetic term remains nonvanishing. On spatially flat FLRW backgrounds with trace torsion, the quadratic actions for perturbations describe one scalar mode and two tensor modes, while the vector perturbations are nondynamical. We identify a nonempty parameter region admitting de Sitter attractors whose scalar and tensor perturbations are free of ghost and gradient instabilities at all momenta.
papers.authors: Jianhui Qiu, Ling-Wei Luo, Chunhui Liu, Chao-Qiang Geng

papers.title: Does the inverse distance ladder rule out late-time solutions to the Hubble tension? A model-independent test using DES-Dovekie supernovae and DESI DR2 BAO
papers.abstract: arXiv:2610.23657v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: It has been argued that the inverse distance ladder disfavours late-time solutions to the Hubble tension. We test this with a cosmographic expansion where $H$ is a fourth-order polynomial in $1 - a$. We combine the uncalibrated DES-Dovekie SNIa with DESI~DR2 BAO, assuming a standard sound horizon $r_{\rm d} = 147.05 \pm 0.30$~Mpc. Using only DES SNIa yields $H_0 = 76.25 \pm 2.87$ km/s/Mpc, which is $3.1\sigma$ above the CMB-calibrated $\Lambda$CDM prediction but consistent with SH0ES ($1.0\sigma$). Adding the legacy SNIa decreases $H_0$ to $67.98 \pm 0.69$ km/s/Mpc, $4.7\sigma$ below SH0ES. The $8.27$ km/s/Mpc drop in $H_0$ upon including the legacy SNIa cannot be attributed to expected sample variance: under a fiducial $\Lambda\text{CDM}$ model, only $1.24\%$ of $10^4$ mock realisations exhibit such a large $H_0$ shift due to the changed redshift sampling. This points to a systematic tension between DES and legacy SNIa datasets. We next add local $H_0$ anchors (the bright siren, SNII, TRGB + SBF) and test a parametrisation where the $\Lambda$CDM $H(z)$ is enhanced by $\Delta H(z) = A \exp (-z/z_1)$. We recover $H_0 = 70.00^{+4.78}_{-0.98}$ km/s/Mpc and $z_1 < 0.086$ at $1\sigma$ confidence using DES SNIa, but $H_0 = 67.66 \pm 1.01$ km/s/Mpc and $z_1$ is unconstrained using DES + legacy. Late-time solutions are thus viable with the homogeneous DES catalogue, but not with the legacy SNIa as published. Allowing them to be arbitrarily recalibrated relative to the main DES sample yields an inferred offset of $\Delta M_\rm{legacy} = 0.0646 \pm 0.0391$~mag, raising the predicted $H_0$ to $71.03 \pm 1.99$ km/s/Mpc. Ongoing SNIa surveys like DEBASS will provide a homogeneous sample of SNIa down to redshifts accessible via the distance ladder, assessing the validity of the current legacy samples and hence the feasibility of late-time solutions to the Hubble tension.
papers.authors: Jos\'e Antonio N\'ajera, Indranil Banik, Harry Desmond

papers.title: The magnetic universe in the theory of gravity with non-minimal kinetic coupling of a scalar field
papers.abstract:
arXiv:2610.23739v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we obtain cosmological solutions within the framework of Bianchi I model with a unidirectional magnetic field in the theory of gravity with non-minimum kinetic coupling of a scalar field with curvature ($\eta\cdot(\phi/2)\cdot G_{\mu
u}\,
abla^\mu 
abla^
u\phi$). We believe that the solutions are applicable to the period before and during primary inflation. In the previous work [R. K. Muharlyamov, T. N. Pankratyeva, S. O. A. Bashir, JCAP05(2025)018] we considered such a problem for a special case -- the locally rotationally symmetric Bianchi I space-time ($a_1=a_2$). Here we generalize the results for different scale factors $a_1
eq a_2 
eq a_3$. There are distinctive properties of the models and a number of interesting properties are preserved. The main conclusion remains valid. For $l=1+\varepsilon\eta \Lambda/\mu>0$, the model has the necessary properties: isotropization during expansion, rapid transition to inflationary expansion, absence of ghost and Laplace instabilities. Here, $\Lambda$ is the cosmological constant, $\mu=M^2_{PL}$ is the Planck mass squared, the sign $\varepsilon=\pm 1$ defines the canonical scalar field and the phantom field, respectively. The differences in the model appear in the neighborhood of the starting point and at times of several units $h_\eta\cdot t$ from it ($h_\eta=\sqrt{ rac{\varepsilon}{3\eta}}$). In the previous model with $l>0$, the Universe is described by the Kasner metric in the neighborhood of the initial point. In the generalized model, there is no the Kasner metric. In the presented model, the anisotropy level is a non-monotonic function. There is a rebound point on the plot. This is the non-standard behavior. But, in the end, the process of isotropization occurs.
papers.authors: Ruslan K. Muharlyamov, Tatiana N. Pankratyeva

papers.title: Runaways in the no-boundary wavefunction
papers.abstract: arXiv:2610.23743v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the no-boundary wavefunction of Einstein gravity with positive cosmological constant. We identify families of weakly curved bulk saddles, including fillings of anisotropic late-time universes $\mathbb{S}^p\times\mathbb{S}^q$, whose weights grow exponentially with geometric parameters of the late-time boundary. These runaways threaten the normalizability of the no-boundary state within gravitational effective field theory. Whether these saddles contribute remains open. Many of the runaway families we study violate the Kontsevich-Segal-Witten criterion, although several are minus asymptotically hyperbolic geometries whose one-loop determinants appear well-defined for pure gravity. For $\mathbb{S}^1\times\mathbb{S}^q$ universes with $q\equiv 0\pmod4$, we construct a contour integral model that excludes the runaway at large $\mathbb{S}^q$.
papers.authors: Jordan Cotler, Prateksh Dhivakar, William Harvey, Victor Ivo, Kristan Jensen

papers.title: Clustering of JWST LRDs. Implications for PBHs and other early-forming seeds
papers.abstract: arXiv:2610.23806v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We use the observed abundance and spatial clustering of JWST little red dots (LRDs) over z = 4--8 to confront two formation scenarios: the standard picture in which LRDs form in virialized dark-matter halos, and one in which they are seeded by a dynamically subdominant population of primordial black holes (PBHs). The halo formation scenario accounts for both observables naturally and without fine-tuning. In the PBH scenario, matching the observed LRD abundance requires a negligibly small PBH mass fraction, and a power-spectrum analysis shows that such a Poisson isocurvature component predicts a clustering signal far below what is observed. The same conclusion holds for any population of dynamically subdominant early-forming seeds, unless their initial clustering is finely tuned or their activity is tied to massive host halos. We conclude that the spatial clustering of JWST LRDs strongly favours the standard halo formation picture and disfavours PBHs, or similar early-forming seeds, as a randomly activated LRD population; PBHs remain viable as seeds only if their activity is governed by massive host halos, in which case clustering alone cannot distinguish them from astrophysical seeds.
papers.authors: Gert H\"utsi

papers.title: Gravitational Waves as a Probe of Multi-Fluid Cosmologies: General Formalism and the Case of Cosmological Stasis
papers.abstract: arXiv:2610.23808v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Scalar-induced gravitational waves (SIGWs) provide a powerful probe of the expansion history of the universe prior to the Big Bang. Indeed, the production of such gravity waves depends on the evolution of first-order scalar perturbations within the early universe, while their subsequent propagation depends on the background equation of state. In this paper we extend previous discussions by studying SIGWs in cosmologies containing multiple fluids. As we shall demonstrate, the gravitational-wave signal within such multi-fluid cosmologies is modified in two distinct ways: not only are there new velocity effects which have no single-fluid analogues, but there are also significant alterations to the subsequent redshifting of modes that enter the horizon before the multi-fluid era ends. Thus SIGWs provide a probe of not only the overall expansion rate within such cosmologies, but also their internal multi-fluid composition. As an example, we then consider the case of gravitational waves arising during an epoch of cosmological stasis. During such an epoch, the abundances of energy components with different equations of state remain constant, thereby giving rise to a universe with a constant effective equation of state which nevertheless remains genuinely multi-fluid despite cosmological expansion. Despite their constant equations of state, we find that such stasis cosmologies also give rise to tensor power spectra and present-day gravitational-wave abundances which are significantly different from those expected within a standard radiation-dominated universe.
papers.authors: Keith R. Dienes, Fazlollah Hajkarim, Lucien Heurtier, Fei Huang, Kuver Sinha, Brooks Thomas, Tao Xu

papers.title: Revisiting the Mass and Scale Dependence of the "Lensing is Low" Effect with DECADE
papers.abstract: arXiv:2610.23828v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Galaxy-galaxy lensing (GGL) is a critical probe of cosmology and galaxy formation. However, predicted GGL amplitudes tend to be $\sim 20-40\%$ higher than observations, primarily on small scales, a tension called the lensing-is-low problem. If not resolved through astrophysics or measurement systematics, this discrepancy may indicate a tension in our cosmological standard model. J. U. Lange et al. (2021), using foreground galaxies from the Baryon Oscillation Spectroscopic Survey (BOSS) and lensing measurements from the Sloan Digital Sky Survey (SDSS), presented evidence that this mismatch extends to large scales where astrophysical explanations are disfavored. We revisit this claim using lensing data from the Dark Energy Camera All Data Everywhere (DECADE) project. Compared to SDSS, the new DECADE measurements reduce the large-scale tension while leaving measurements on small scales mostly unchanged. Ultimately, these new results favor a scale dependence in the lensing-is-low problem.
papers.authors: Kimiko Queen, Abigail V. Fisher, Johannes U. Lange
